This release fixes one security issue in ConcurrencyLimitedModel. See the advisory for full details and affected versions.

  • GHSA-6fqq-452j-qhrp (high): a streamed request through ConcurrencyLimitedModel or limit_model_concurrency could keep its concurrency slot when the slot was released on a different task than the one that acquired it: after an early exit (the consumer stopped iterating, raised, or was cancelled), and also after fully consuming stream_text() with its default debouncing. Repeated streams could then block every request sharing the limiter. Agent-level max_concurrency and non-streaming requests are not affected. Reported by @​lche511. (#9478)

The fix also changes how limiters are shared: a model wrapper now raises UserError when it shares a limiter with the agent making the request or with an enclosing model wrapper, ConcurrencyLimiter.acquire() takes a slot on every call, even on the same task, and a custom AbstractConcurrencyLimiter must allow release() from another task.

Patched in 2.53.0. v1 is not affected.

title: 🐛 Fix regression when using `str` with `Form()`
body:
## Pull Request

Discussion: Closes https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/discussions/14471

## Description

Closes https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/discussions/14471

This fixes a regression introduced in version 0.123.2. After upgrading one of my projects, endpoints suddenly started throwing `HTTP 422` responses due to empty string form values being passed. The key was definitely being passed, but because it was empty, it was being treated as if it wasn't passed at all. Fixing this would require adding `= ""` to all my string based form endpoints, which is a lot.

The long term solution is to fix the regression itself. This commit adds an explicit check for empty string values on fields which have an explicit string type. If both conditions are met, an empty string is used instead of `None`, as it was pre-regression.

title: 📝 Add a section on handling errors inside background tasks
body:
This picks up #14599, which the inactivity bot closed while I was away — my fault for going quiet. The
bot suggested opening a new PR, so here it is, rewritten rather than restored.

The gap: a background task that raises cannot change a response that has already been sent, and the
exception never reaches the path operation function. From the outside a failed task looks exactly like
a successful one. #2505, #2604 and #3589 all come back to that, and the tutorial does not mention it.

What changed since the earlier attempt, after reading how the rest of the docs are written:

- the example moved into `docs_src/background_tasks/tutorial003_py310.py` and is referenced with
  `{* ... *}`, so it is covered by a test like the other examples rather than being an inline block
- `/// tip` instead of `!!! tip`, which is what the other 37 files in the tutorial use
- the heading is "Handle errors in the task", matching the sentence-case style of its neighbours
- the section is shorter, and points at the existing [Caveat](#caveat) rather than repeating it

Two tests in `tests/test_tutorial/test_background_tasks/test_tutorial003.py`: the example runs, and a
task that raises still returns 200 while the error reaches the log — which is the behaviour the section
is actually describing. `5 passed` in that directory.

Happy to trim it further if it is more than you want in a tutorial page.

title: ✅ Add unit tests for is_body_allowed_for_status_code
body:
## Summary

Add direct unit test coverage for `fastapi.utils.is_body_allowed_for_status_code`.

This small helper decides, per the OpenAPI Specification's patterned fields, whether responses may carry a body. It is used by `fastapi/exception_handlers.py` and `fastapi/openapi/utils.py`, but it had no direct test coverage: the `204/205/304` (and `1XX` numeric edge) behaviour was only pinned implicitly through request-level tests.

The new file `tests/test_is_body_allowed_for_status_code.py` pins three groups of expectations:

- `None` and the patterned codes `default`, `1XX`, `2XX`, `3XX`, `4XX`, `5XX` allow a body.
- `100`, `199`, `204`, `205`, `304` (as `int` and as `str`) do **not** allow a body.
- All other regular codes (`200`, `201`, `300`, `301`, `302`, `400`, `404`, `500`, incl. string forms) allow a body.

Behaviour tested is the current implementation (comment in the source already references the OpenAPI spec); no production code is changed.

## Verification

- `uv run pytest tests/test_is_body_allowed_for_status_code.py -q` → `29 passed in 0.34s`
- `uv run ruff format --check tests/test_is_body_allowed_for_status_code.py` → `1 file already formatted`

title: Docs: note that native OpenTelemetry works on AWS Lambda (Mangum)
body:
### Summary

The new OpenTelemetry page (https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/advanced/opentelemetry/) doesn't mention serverless / AWS Lambda. I tried it there and it works with only the documented env vars, so a short note would help others wondering about flushing on Lambda.

### Verified setup

- FastAPI `0.142.2` installed as `fastapi[standard]`, no other app code or OTel SDK/instrumentation packages added
- Wrapped with [Mangum](https://github.com/Kludex/mangum) (`handler = Mangum(app)`), AWS Lambda container image, behind API Gateway (HTTP API)
- Only env vars set on the function: `OTEL_SERVICE_NAME`, `OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES`, `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT`, `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS` (Grafana Cloud OTLP gateway, Basic auth)
- No explicit `force_flush` / shutdown hook in the app

### Result

Request traces and metrics from the Lambda-hosted app arrive and are visible in Grafana Cloud.

### Suggested docs change

Add a short "Serverless / AWS Lambda" note to the OpenTelemetry page, e.g.: auto-configuration works unchanged on Lambda via an ASGI adapter such as Mangum, just set the `OTEL_*` env vars on the function.

### Open question

I haven't looked at why no explicit flush is needed (processor choice, flush on shutdown, or something else). If there are cases where it does matter (e.g. very short invocations, Lambda SnapStart, other adapters), it would be good for the docs to say so. I only verified the setup above.

datetime fields now use UTCDateTime, a custom type based on DateTime(timezone=True). Plain datetime validation still accepts both aware and naive values, but naive database parameters now raise an error.

Explicit SQLAlchemy types retain their existing behavior. PostgreSQL needs a column migration that explicitly specifies the timezone of existing values. SQLite and MySQL/MariaDB keep their column definitions, but existing non-UTC values need a data migration before adopting the new type. Update datetime producers, query parameters, comparisons, and any database defaults to follow the new UTC convention.

title: 🐛 Fix stale Content-Length in 205 Reset Content responses
body:
## Summary

A path operation that uses status `205 Reset Content` and returns anything (even `None`) produces a response whose `Content-Length` header doesn't match its (empty) body. Under Uvicorn every such request fails and the client receives a truncated response.

This PR sets `Content-Length: 0` when FastAPI drops the body of a 205 response. No other status code is affected.

## Reproduction

```python
from fastapi import FastAPI

app = FastAPI()


@app.post("/reset", status_code=205)
def reset():
    return None
```

Run it with `uvicorn main:app` and send a request:

```console
$ curl -v -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/reset
< HTTP/1.1 205 Reset Content
< content-length: 4
* transfer closed with 4 bytes remaining to read
```

Uvicorn logs the following for **every** request:

```
RuntimeError: Response content shorter than Content-Length
```

The same happens when the status is set dynamically through the `Response` parameter:

```python
from fastapi import FastAPI, Response

app = FastAPI()


@app.post("/reset")
def reset(response: Response):
    response.status_code = 205
    return {"message": "Form submitted"}
```

Here the header is `content-length: 28` while the body is empty.

**Expected:** a valid 205 response with `content-length: 0` and an empty body, so the connection can be reused.

**Actual:** `content-length` is the length of the serialized return value, the body is empty, the server errors and the connection is dropped.

## Root cause

In `get_request_handler()` (`fastapi/routing.py`), the response is built first and the body is dropped afterwards for status codes that must not have one:

```python
response = actual_response_class(content, **response_args)
if not is_body_allowed_for_status_code(response.status_code):
    response.body = b""
```

By the time `response.body` is cleared, the response class has already computed `Content-Length` from the original content (e.g. `4` for `null`), so the header goes stale.

This only causes a mismatch for 205. Starlette's `Response.init_headers()` already skips `Content-Length` for status codes below 200 and for 204 and 304, so for those there is no header to go stale. 205 is the only status FastAPI treats as "no body" (`is_body_allowed_for_status_code()` returns `False` for `< 200`, 204, 205 and 304) that Starlette still adds a `Content-Length` for.

## The fix

```python
if not is_body_allowed_for_status_code(response.status_code):
    response.body = b""
    # Unlike 1xx, 204, and 304, a 205 response is still
    # delimited by Content-Length, so it has to match the
    # now empty body
    # Ref: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9112#section-6.3
    if response.status_code == 205:
        response.headers["content-length"] = "0"
```

The change runs before the headers from the `Response` parameter are appended, so it only corrects the value computed by the response class and never overrides a header set explicitly by the user.

## Why only 205 (re: #16386)

#16386 tried to fix the same bug and was closed with the concern that the change might break something else, specifically 304 responses, which may legitimately carry a `Content-Length`. This PR is scoped to address that:

- **RFC 9112 §6.3** (message body length): any response with a 1xx, 204 or 304 status is always terminated by the first empty line after the header fields, *regardless of the header fields present*. So for those, `Content-Length` doesn't affect framing, and they are left untouched.
- **205 is not in that list**, so its body length is determined by `Content-Length`. If the header says 4 and no bytes follow, the message is malformed. That's exactly the error Uvicorn reports.
- **RFC 9110 §15.3.6**: a server must not generate content in a 205 response. With `Content-Length: 0` the response is correct and the connection stays reusable.
- **RFC 9110 §8.6**: a server may send `Content-Length` in a 304 with the size of the representation that a 200 would have returned. This PR does not touch 304, and a test confirms that a `Content-Length` set by the user on a 304 is preserved.

Why `0` rather than removing the header: without `Content-Length` or `Transfer-Encoding: chunked`, an HTTP/1.1 client has to read until the connection closes to know where the response ends, which breaks keep-alive. An explicit `Content-Length: 0` is the unambiguous way to frame an empty 205.

## Tests

New file `tests/test_response_code_no_body_content_length.py`:

| Test | Before the fix | After the fix |
|---|---|---|
| 205 via `status_code=205`, returning a dict | ❌ `content-length: 28` | ✅ `0` |
| 205 via `status_code=205`, returning `None` | ❌ `content-length: 4` | ✅ `0` |
| 205 set through the `Response` parameter | ❌ `content-length: 28` | ✅ `0` |
| 304 with a user-set `Content-Length: 17` | ✅ kept | ✅ kept |

Also checked:

- The existing test suite passes, including `test_response_code_no_body.py` and the tutorial tests.
- `ruff check`, `ruff format --check` and `mypy` pass on the changed files.
- Manually verified with Uvicorn: the 205 response now has `content-length: 0`, no error is logged and the connection stays open.

## Scope and compatibility

- 6 lines in `fastapi/routing.py`, only on the code path where FastAPI already drops the body.
- No public API changes.
- Responses returned directly from the endpoint (a `Response` instance) are not affected, since they don't go through this path.
- Behavior only changes for 205 responses, which were broken before.

title: 🐛 Ensure SSE endpoint generators and checkpoint streams are closed on client disconnect
body:
### Discussion

- Proposed and confirmed in Discussion: https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/discussions/16346

---

### Description

In `fastapi/routing.py`, when handling Server-Sent Events (`EventSourceResponse`), the `_producer` task consumes `sse_aiter` and forwards events to `send_stream`.

When a client disconnects while the producer is awaiting `send_stream.send(...)`, the task group cancels the producer task. Because `sse_aiter` was never explicitly closed upon cancellation, the generator's `finally` cleanup block (e.g. database session teardown, locks, or external resources) would not run deterministically until garbage collection or loop termination.

This PR:
1. Wraps `_producer` iteration in a `try/finally` block that explicitly awaits `sse_aiter.aclose()` inside a shielded cancel scope.
2. Catches `anyio.BrokenResourceError` and `anyio.ClosedResourceError` in `_producer` and `_keepalive_inserter` so stream cancellation unwinds cleanly across both `asyncio` and `trio`.
3. Registers `sse_stream_content.aclose` on the request's `async_exit_stack` to guarantee `_sse_with_checkpoints` is closed during request teardown without leaking unexhausted async generators.
4. Adds regression test `test_sse_generator_closed_on_disconnect_while_send_blocked` to `tests/test_sse.py`.

title: 🐛 Fix 500 instead of 422 when validation errors contain non-finite floats
body:
Fixes the client-triggerable 500 reported in #16405.

When a JSON body contains a non-finite float literal (`NaN`, `Infinity`, `-Infinity`, accepted by `json.loads` by default) and the target field rejects it, a plain `int`, `FiniteFloat`, or a float with `allow_inf_nan=False`, the `RequestValidationError` payload embeds the raw invalid input (`"input": nan`). `jsonable_encoder` passes floats through verbatim, and `JSONResponse.render` serializes with `json.dumps(allow_nan=False)`, so rendering the 422 raises `ValueError: Out of range float values are not JSON compliant` and the client receives a 500.

The fix encodes non-finite floats in the validation error payload as their `repr` strings (`"nan"`, `"inf"`, `"-inf"`) using the existing `custom_encoder` support of `jsonable_encoder`, scoped to `request_validation_exception_handler` only:

- finite floats in `input` remain numbers
- normal application responses are unaffected
- nested non-finite inputs are covered, since `jsonable_encoder` applies `custom_encoder` on each recursive call

The websocket handler is intentionally not touched: it passes the encoded payload as the close `reason`, which does not go through `JSONResponse.render`, so it cannot raise this error.

Regression tests in `tests/test_nonfinite_validation_errors.py` cover `NaN`, `Infinity`, `-Infinity`, `FiniteFloat`, a nested dict input, a finite float staying numeric, and the valid-request path.

Credit: the `custom_encoder` approach was proposed by @mmaxjr in #16405.

title: Use an explicit response_model as the item type on streaming endpoints
body:
Discussed in https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/discussions/16382.

On a streaming (generator) endpoint, `response_model` is only turned into a per-item field when it is left to the return annotation. Passing it explicitly silently disables both validation and the `response_model_*` options, and leaves the OpenAPI `itemSchema` empty:

```python
class Item(BaseModel):
    name: str
    secret: str

@app.get("/stream", response_model=Item, response_model_exclude={"secret"})
def stream():
    yield Item(name="public", secret="private")
```

Before this change the endpoint streams `{"name": "public", "secret": "private"}`, so a field the developer asked to exclude is served to the client, and the OpenAPI response is `{"application/jsonl": {"itemSchema": {}}}`. Writing `response_model=Iterable[Item]` instead does not help: it is rejected outright as an invalid response field.

`_populate_api_route_state` resolves the stream item type only inside the `isinstance(response_model, DefaultPlaceholder)` branch. With an explicit model, `route.stream_item_type` stays `None`, `stream_item_field` is never built, and `_serialize_data` falls back to `jsonable_encoder` plus `json.dumps`, which is the path that skips validation and the exclusion options.

An explicit `response_model` on a streaming endpoint now feeds `stream_item_field` the same way the return annotation does, and both the item type and an iterable of it are accepted. Afterwards the endpoint above streams `{"name": "public"}` and its OpenAPI response carries `itemSchema: {"$ref": "#/components/schemas/Item"}`.

The new branch only applies to generator endpoints whose response class is the default placeholder (JSONL) or `EventSourceResponse` (SSE), and it keeps the existing `ServerSentEvent` exclusion, since that is a transport wrapper rather than a data model. Non-streaming endpoints, bare iterables and return-annotation streams are untouched.

## Tests

`tests/test_stream_explicit_response_model.py` covers sync and async generators, `Iterable[Item]` and `AsyncIterable[Item]`, `response_model_exclude` and `response_model_exclude_none`, SSE, per-item validation, and the OpenAPI schema, together with a non-streaming endpoint to pin that its behaviour is unchanged. On `master` the module fails at import, because `response_model=Iterable[Item]` raises `FastAPIError`.

The rest of the suite passes: 2046 passed, 12 skipped (`tests/`, excluding `benchmarks` and `test_tutorial`, which need optional extras not installed here).

title: 🐛 Prevent stale endpoint context cache entries
body:
## Problem

`_extract_endpoint_context()` caches endpoint metadata by `id(func)` without retaining or validating the function object. After an endpoint is collected, Python can reuse that id for another endpoint, causing validation errors and logs to report the wrong file, line, or function.

## Solution

Store a weak reference alongside each cached context and validate the referenced object with `is` before using a cache hit. Callable objects that do not support weak references are still handled correctly and are recomputed instead of being retained.

title: 👷 Fix coverage badge: keep Smokeshow HTML under size limit and fail on upload errors
body:
The coverage badge in the README currently shows `coverage ??%`. The badge worker reports:

```
No status found which matched regex ^coverage, status descriptions: []
```

No `smokeshow / coverage` status has been posted on `master` since #14992 (2026-02-27). The last commits before it (e.g. 4fce9ce, 728b097) have `Coverage 100.00%`; every code commit after it has none.

## Root cause

#14992 replaced coverage's `dynamic_context = "test_function"` with pytest-cov's `--cov-context=test`. pytest-cov records one context per parametrized case **and** per phase (`|setup`, `|run`, `|teardown`), e.g.:

```
Linux-py3.13-no-deprecation|tests/test_request_params/test_cookie/test_optional_str.py::test_optional_alias_by_alias[/optional-alias]|run
```

The combined data now has ~20k contexts, and with `show_contexts = true` the generated `htmlcov` grew to **~68 MB**, over Smokeshow's 50 MB site limit. Every upload fails with:

```
ERROR! ... status=429 response=429: You've exceeded the site size limit of 52428800.
```

Since the status is only posted after a successful upload, it's never set.

This went unnoticed because the retry loop in `smokeshow.yml` ends with `sleep 1` when all 5 attempts fail, so the step exits 0 and the Smokeshow workflow is green.

## Changes

* `test.yml`: generate the HTML report with `--omit "tests/*"`. This keeps the per-test contexts for `fastapi/` and `docs_src/` (the useful part, "which test covers this line"), while dropping the per-file pages for the test files themselves. `coverage report --fail-under=100` is unchanged and still checks tests.
* `smokeshow.yml`: exit with an error if all upload attempts fail, so this kind of breakage is visible.

## Verification

Using the coverage artifacts from the latest `master` Test run (50113da):

| | HTML size | total |
|---|---|---|
| current | 68 MB | 100% |
| with `--omit "tests/*"` | 35 MB | 100% |

(For reference, disabling `show_contexts` entirely gives 41 MB; this approach keeps contexts and leaves more headroom.)

Also checked the upload loop with a stubbed command: exits `1` when every attempt fails, `0` on success.

title: _endpoint_context_cache keyed by id(func) can return stale context after GC
body:
### Bug

`_extract_endpoint_context()` in `fastapi/routing.py` caches per-endpoint context in `_endpoint_context_cache: dict[int, EndpointContext]` keyed by `id(func)`, holding only the `ctx` dict with no reference to `func`.

After the endpoint function is garbage-collected, CPython reuses the address for a new function object, and the cache returns the old endpoint's `file`/`line`/`function`. The cache is also never cleared, so it grows unbounded.

### Repro (fastapi 0.141.1, Python 3.14.4, Linux)

```python
import gc
from fastapi.routing import _extract_endpoint_context

def endpoint_alpha():
    pass

ctx_a = _extract_endpoint_context(endpoint_alpha)
id_a = id(endpoint_alpha)
del endpoint_alpha
gc.collect()

for i in range(50000):
    g = {}
    exec(f'def endpoint_beta_{i}():\n    pass\n', g)
    fn = g[f'endpoint_beta_{i}']
    if id(fn) == id_a:
        break
    del fn, g

stale = _extract_endpoint_context(fn)
print(stale.get('function'), '| actual:', fn.__name__)
assert stale.get('function') == fn.__name__, f"STALE: {stale} vs {fn.__name__}"
```

Output on my machine:

```
endpoint_alpha | actual: endpoint_beta_0
AssertionError: STALE: {...'function': 'endpoint_alpha'...} vs endpoint_beta_0
```

(The exact `endpoint_beta_N` index varies per run; id reuse triggered on the first try here.)

### Expected / actual

- Expected: context always describes the function passed in.
- Actual: a recycled `id()` returns another endpoint's `file`/`line`/`function`, so validation-error messages and logs can point at the wrong endpoint.

### Environment

- fastapi 0.141.1 (also present on current `master`, `fastapi/routing.py:275-297`)
- Python 3.14.4, Linux

### Possible fix direction

Validate the hit against func identity instead of trusting the bare `id()` — e.g. store `(func, ctx)` and compare with `is`, key the cache by the function object itself (or a weak reference), or drop the hand-rolled dict for a bounded cache. Related PR #16387 fixes the shared-mutation half with `.copy()` but leaves this key-recycling half in place.

title: fix: serialize WebSocket validation errors to JSON string in close reason
body:
The default `websocket_request_validation_exception_handler` currently passes the result of `jsonable_encoder(exc.errors())` directly to `WebSocket.close()` as the `reason`.

`jsonable_encoder(exc.errors())` returns a list, while `WebSocket.close()` expects `reason` to be a `str | None`. As a result, WebSocket request-validation errors can cause the exception handler itself to fail instead of closing the connection with the intended `1008` policy-violation code.

This change serializes the validation errors with `json.dumps()` before passing them to `WebSocket.close()`. The reason is therefore a valid string containing machine-readable JSON.

A regression test was added to verify that:

- WebSocket request-validation failures close with code `1008`.
- The close reason is a string.
- The reason contains the expected validation error.
- The behavior fails with the previous implementation and passes with this fix.

The change is intentionally minimal and does not alter the validation behavior or the WebSocket close code.

body:

Discussion: https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/discussions/16382

## Description

When specifying an explicit `response_model` (such as `response_model=Item`, `response_model=Iterator[Item]`, or `response_model=AsyncIterable[Item]`) on generator streaming endpoints (JSONL and SSE), it was ignored during response serialization and generated an empty OpenAPI `itemSchema: {}`.

### Root Cause
In `_populate_api_route_state()`, `get_stream_item_type()` was only called when `response_model` was an instance of `DefaultPlaceholder`. When an explicit `response_model` was provided:
1. `route.stream_item_type` was never populated, leaving `stream_item_field` as `None`.
2. `route.response_field` was erroneously populated instead.
3. At runtime, streaming endpoints serialize items via `stream_item_field`. Because it was `None`, serialization fell back to `jsonable_encoder()`, bypassing model validation and field filters (`response_model_include`, `response_model_exclude`, `response_model_exclude_none`).
4. OpenAPI generation emitted an empty `itemSchema: {}` because `stream_item_field` was absent.

### Fix
In `_populate_api_route_state()`:
- Check if the route is a streaming generator (`is_sse_stream` or `is_json_stream`) with an explicit `response_model`.
- Extract the item model using `get_stream_item_type(response_model) or response_model`.
- If it is not `ServerSentEvent`, assign `route.stream_item_type = stream_item`.
- Set `response_model = None` so `stream_item_field` is created for per-item serialization, validation, and OpenAPI generation.

### Tests Added
Added `tests/test_stream_response_model.py` covering:
- Async JSONL stream with explicit model and field filtering (`response_model_exclude`, `response_model_exclude_none`)
- Async JSONL stream with `response_model=AsyncIterable[Item]`
- Sync generator JSONL stream with `response_model=Iterator[Item]`
- SSE stream with explicit model and field exclusion
- SSE stream yielding `ServerSentEvent` directly
- SSE stream with explicit `response_model=ServerSentEvent`
- Non-streaming endpoints unaffected
- Validation error raised on invalid yielded chunk in async stream
- Validation error raised on invalid yielded chunk in sync stream
- Router inclusion via `app.include_router()`
- OpenAPI schema generation (`itemSchema` for JSONL and `contentSchema` for SSE)

title: Unwrap Annotated layers in get_stream_item_type for streaming return annotations
body:
### Discussion

- Proposed and confirmed in Discussion: https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/discussions/16379

---

### Description

In `fastapi/dependencies/utils.py`, `get_stream_item_type(annotation)` checks if the annotation is a subclass or instance of `AsyncIterator` or `AsyncGenerator`.

However, when a route endpoint uses `Annotated[...]` in its return type annotation (e.g. `Annotated[AsyncIterator[str], ...]` or `Annotated[AsyncGenerator[str, None], ...]`), `get_stream_item_type` failed to inspect the inner stream type because `get_origin(annotation)` returns `Annotated` rather than unwrapping to the inner origin type. As a result, FastAPI fell back to non-streaming response handling.

This PR unwraps any outer/nested `Annotated` type layers using `get_args(annotation)[0]` before checking `issubclass(origin, (AsyncIterator, AsyncGenerator))`.

title: ⚡️ Avoid importing pydantic.v1 in Pydantic v2-only apps
body:
Follow-up to discussion #16355.

## Problem

Registering the first route imports the whole `pydantic.v1` package, even in an app that only uses Pydantic v2:

```
app.py                         @app.get("/items")
  fastapi/routing.py             add_api_route -> get_dependant -> analyze_param
    fastapi/utils.py               annotation_is_pydantic_v1(type_)
      fastapi/_compat/shared.py      from pydantic import v1
```

Since #14609 dropped `pydantic.v1` support, both callers of this detection (`fastapi/utils.py` and `fastapi/encoders.py`) exist only to raise `PydanticV1NotSupportedError`. For a v2-only app the answer is always `False`, and the import is never used for anything else. The `encoders.py` call site can also hit it during request serialization for any object that falls through `ENCODERS_BY_TYPE`.

Cost measured on FastAPI 0.141.1 / Pydantic 2.13.5 / CPython 3.14:

| | |
|---|---|
| AWS Lambda, arm64, 512 MB, cold start | **44 ms** median of 5 |
| Local, warm bytecode, `fastapi` and `pydantic` already imported | 4.2 ms median of 5 |
| On disk | 1.2 MB |

## Change

A `pydantic.v1` model class cannot exist unless `pydantic.v1` has already been imported, so `"pydantic.v1" in sys.modules` is a necessary condition for either detection function to ever return `True`. Both `is_pydantic_v1_model_class` and `is_pydantic_v1_model_instance` now return `False` early when that key is absent, before touching the import.

Behavior is unchanged for anyone who does define a v1 model: they imported `pydantic.v1` to do so, so they still get `PydanticV1NotSupportedError` with the same message. The only way to bypass the check is deleting `sys.modules["pydantic.v1"]` after defining a model, which is not a supported pattern.

## Tests

Two tests added to `tests/test_compat.py`, both using `monkeypatch.delitem(sys.modules, "pydantic.v1", raising=False)` so they are independent of test order:

- unit: both detection functions return `False` for a v2 model and `pydantic.v1` stays out of `sys.modules`
- integration: an app with a v2 body model handles a request end to end without importing `pydantic.v1`

The existing `tests/test_pydantic_v1_error.py` still passes, covering the branch after the guard.
